title: Separating basis construction and transfer in an algebraic field diamond
statement: Let $k_0\subseteq k\subseteq E$ and $k_0\subseteq F\subseteq E$ be inclusions of fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]; $k$ and $F$ need not contain one another. Assume that $k/k_0$ is algebraic, that $E/F$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], that both $E/k_0$ and $F/k_0$ are finitely generated as fields, and that for every extension field $L/k_0$ the ring $F\otimes_{k_0}L$ is reduced. Algebraic means that every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the base; finitely generated means generated as a field by finitely many elements; reduced means having no nonzero nilpotents. The tensor product is the commutative algebra tensor product, with $(f\otimes l)(f'\otimes l')=ff'\otimes ll'$. Let $d\in\mathbf N$ satisfy $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}F=d$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There are $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in F$ forming a transcendence basis of $F/k_0$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that $F/k_0(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is separable algebraic, the family is algebraically independent over $k$, and $E/k(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is finite separable. Finite separable means finite-dimensional and separable algebraic; the generated subfields are taken inside $E$. The empty family is allowed when $d=0$.

proof.text: Choose a separating transcendence basis of $F/k_0$. In characteristic zero apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis]. In characteristic $p>0$, reducedness of every $F\otimes_{k_0}L$ gives [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable]; since $F/k_0$ is finitely generated, apply its conclusion to $F$ itself and unfold [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension](1)-(2). In both cases [def-kun-transcendence-degree] identifies the cardinality of this basis with $d$, so enumerate it as $t_1,\ldots,t_d$. Set $A=k_0(t_1,\ldots,t_d)\subseteq F$ and $B=k(t_1,\ldots,t_d)\subseteq E$. We have $F/A$ separable algebraic.

The family $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, viewed in $E$, is algebraically independent over $k_0$: a polynomial relation in $E$ is the identical relation in the subfield $F$. Apply [lem-zl-independence-algebraic-base] to the tower $k_0\subseteq k\subseteq E$ and the assumed algebraicity of $k/k_0$. The family is therefore algebraically independent over $k$.

source.place: Algebraic-base independence as recorded by lem-zl-independence-algebraic-base; Mathlib/RingTheory/AlgebraicIndependent/AlgebraicClosure.lean:96-98.

proof.text: In the tower $A\subseteq F\subseteq E$, both successive extensions are separable algebraic: $F/A$ by step 1 and $E/F$ by hypothesis. Thus [lem-zl-separable-permanence] gives $E/A$ separable algebraic.

Since $k_0\subseteq k$ and every $t_i$ lies in $B$, the defining minimality of a generated subfield gives $A\subseteq B\subseteq E$. Every element of $B$ is algebraic over $A$, because it lies in $E$ and step 3 makes $E/A$ algebraic; likewise each polynomial over $A$ witnessing algebraicity of an element of $E$ remains nonzero over $B$. Thus this is a tower of algebraic field extensions, as required by the Stacks source. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base] to this tower and step 3: $E/B$ is separable algebraic. This application requires no inclusion between $k$ and $F$.

Write $E=k_0(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ using finite generation over $k_0$. Because $k_0\subseteq B\subseteq E$, generated-subfield minimality gives $E=B(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. Step 4 makes each $a_i$ algebraic over $B$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] over $B$ proves $[E:B]<\infty$. Together with steps 1, 2 and 4 this is every asserted clause. For $d=0$ the generated fields are $A=k_0$ and $B=k$, and the same argument uses the empty family without any change.
